title: Palindrome Detection
domain: STRING! values compared as exact, case-sensitive bytes; no Unicode normalisation or case folding.
description: Return 1 when a STRING! reads the same in both directions, else 0. The proposed implementation used the unbound words true/false; the verified version uses Glon's existing 1/0 Boolean convention. Comparison is exact byte equality, not REBOL's default case-insensitive string equality and not character-aware Unicode reversal.
attribution: Problem and REBOL reference: Rosetta Code, 'Palindrome detection' (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Palindrome_detection). The REBOL listing is the extended published solution shown on that page; the Glon implementation is the proposed version with the Boolean correction.
reference: Expected values are generated independently by Python byte-sequence reversal (b == b[::-1]), including case-sensitive text, binary-safe NUL/high-byte cases and deterministic random byte strings.
family_note: Rosetta Code challenge; separate from REBOL Cookbook challenges.

resource_probes.observed: exit 1; machine halt before output (return-stack exhaustion); no SIN!
resource_probes.note: Recursive-depth probe. A 160-byte constructed palindrome passes; 200 bytes (100 recursive pairs) fail-stops. Not a correctness case and not a search for the maximum.

known_limitations: The proposed true/false words are not bound in the pinned prelude; the verified implementation returns 1/0, the existing Glon Boolean convention.

Glon compares exact bytes with s/raw-at. REBOL's extended palindrome? defaults to case-insensitive string equality and only uses exact comparison with /case; REBOL reverse operates on characters, while Glon works on bytes. No Unicode normalisation or case folding is added.
Recursive depth grows by one activation per compared pair. A 160-byte palindrome passes; a 200-byte palindrome fail-stops with return-stack exhaustion (machine halt, not SIN!).
The page's separate minimalistic REBOL one-liner is malformed/truncated as published; the extended valid solution is the reference.

reference_implementation.title: Palindrome detection — extended REBOL solution shown on Rosetta Code
reference_implementation.attribution: Rosetta Code, Palindrome detection, REBOL solution (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Palindrome_detection).
reference_implementation.notes: Extended solution with /case exact comparison and /ignore inexact detection, plus the published test suite.

rebol.observable_behaviour: palindrome? uses case-insensitive string equality by default; palindrome?/case uses exact comparison; inexact-palindrome? ignores selected punctuation/space characters.
rebol.facilities: func refinements, ==/= string comparison, reverse, copy, charset, parse and all from REBOL 2.
rebol.test_status: The extended published listing is preserved verbatim as reference source. It was not executed here; there is no REBOL 2 runtime in this repository.

glon.observable_behaviour: Returns 1/0 for exact, case-sensitive byte equality; no inexact/punctuation- ignoring variant is introduced.
glon.facilities: Ordinary Glon func/either, >= and =, arithmetic, s/length, s/raw-at and recursion; no new vocabulary or runtime change.
glon.test_status: All committed exact-output cases passed on the pinned interpreter; deterministic Python byte reversal supplied expected values. A 200-byte resource probe records the recursion limit.

implementation_comparison.notice: The REBOL reference includes a separate inexact mode and a case-insensitive default; the Glon challenge intentionally implements only the exact case-sensitive byte contract. Both core functions are application-level recursive definitions; source sizes are descriptive, not a concision claim.
